title: Every odd antihole is strongly chromatic-choosable: paper, Lean 4 formalization and verification code
description:
We prove Conjecture 9 of A. Fiujlaali and J. McDonald (arXiv:2610.14241): for every l >= 3 the odd antihole on 2l-1 vertices, the complement of the cycle of length 2l-1, is strongly l-chromatic-choosable, that is, its chromatic number is l and the only assignments of lists of size l-1 from which it cannot be coloured are the constant ones. With their Theorem 10 this proves their Conjecture 3: an odd-hole-free k-critical graph of maximum degree D containing an odd antihole of length 2(D-k)+7 is that antihole.

preprintOddAntiholeConjecture/ holds the paper as a PDF; paper/ holds the LaTeX source (amsart) with four schematic figures; dist/ holds the PDF, the LaTeX source zip and the arXiv tarball; MasterOddAntiholeConjecture_masterzipfinal2.zip holds every file of the repository. lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib project that proves the main theorem odd_antihole_strongly_chromatic_choosable together with every lemma it rests on (Hall's theorem in the form used, the Erdos-Rubin-Taylor lemma, the key lemma on a single path, the path theorem for odd linear forests and the cycle theorem); it depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. checks/ contains independent checks in C, C++, Julia and Python; the C check examines every assignment of lists of size l-1, up to renaming the colours, for l = 3 (4,900 assignments) and l = 4 (7,897,749,769 assignments). scripts/run_all.sh builds the Lean project, checks the axioms and runs the checks. The deduction of Conjecture 3 follows Fiujlaali and McDonald and is proved by hand in the paper.
